normalized.governing_thought: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon. Do not launch 600 retail doors, and hold the Japan scale-up for a later year
executive_summary: Recommendation: approve Option A (Amazon-led) for 2027 with a $4M US cash envelope. Reject Option B (600-door retail launch) and defer Option J (Japan scale-up). Add specialty retail only once aided awareness passes 20%.
The US is worth entering: US K-beauty skincare reached $3.6B in 2025, growing 17% a year against 5% for all facial skincare
41% of it sells on Amazon, and 61% of K-beauty buyers buy there most often
The pilot works: monthly units +89% in six months, 4.5 stars, repeat close to benchmark (29% vs 31%)
Only Amazon-led fits the board's limits: Retail-led breaks the $18M cap (−$20.8M peak), never pays back and pulls group margin to 4.5%, even on its own inputs
Those inputs are optimistic: brands at Onsoo's awareness sell 2.6 units/door/week; the retailer removes brands below 4.0
Amazon-led needs $1.9–3.9M of peak cash and keeps group margin at 9% or more
What the board has to accept: Payback by 2030 holds only if ACoS stays at or below 28.6%. At the 32% scaling benchmark it slips to about 2032
No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the limits. Option A reaches ~$26M; reset $40M as a 2031–32 milestone
Guardrails on ad cost, cash and repeat purchase bring the decision back to the board early

1.1%: Share of 2025 K-beauty skincare sales that the $40M ambition represents

survey of 1,200 US women 18–44, Sep 2026 (K-beauty buyer sub-sample)

slides.title: The Amazon pilot shows growing demand: monthly units nearly doubled in six months at 4.5 stars

evidence: Jan 7.4, Feb 8.6, Mar 10.1, Apr 11.8, May 12.9, Jun 14.0

slides.title: An Amazon unit earns $4.73 at the planned 25% ad cost but only $3.05 at the 32% benchmark. Retail earns more per unit but carries far more fixed cost

Retail's fixed-cost problem

The plan has 600 doors in 2027, selling 140k units

claims.claim: Ads are the largest controllable Amazon cost: each point of ACoS = $0.24 a unit

Group operating margin (floor 8%), 2027–2030

In return its retail leg earns $1.1–1.8M a year and the assumed Amazon halo $0.4–1.6M

slides.title: And B's inputs are optimistic: at Onsoo's awareness, newcomer brands sell about 2.6 units per door a week, well below the 4.0 the retailer requires

slides.title: Option A pays back by 2030 only if ad cost stays at or below 28.6% of sales. Above that, payback slips, but the cash at risk stays small

claims.claim: Cumulative cash at end-2030 by ACoS, $M (Duty 15% today / Duty 25% review)
Break-even ACoS is 28.6%, or 26.9% if the duty rises to 25%. The pilot ran at 28%
The plan assumes ACoS falls to 25%; the benchmark says it rises with scale as click costs climb
evidence: agency benchmark: median ACoS 32% (range 26–38%) for brands scaling $5M→$20M on Amazon US

claims.claim: In every case peak cash stays ≤ $7.5M and group margin ≥ 8.7%

slides.title: If Amazon stalls the way it did for two peers, Option A loses about $7M. A retail-first failure costs three times that

claims.claim: Peak cumulative cash need through 2030, $M
Recent K-beauty entrants
evidence: Saebom: Amazon-first 2022, ~$30M revenue in 2025; added 300 doors
Mooncrest: Retail-first 2023, 450 doors, Removed in 2025; est. $21M loss

claims.claim: Amazon-first does not guarantee scale: two of three peers stayed below $5M. But that failure is cheap and shows early, so it can be stopped. The retail-first failure cost more than Onsoo's whole cap.
evidence: Stall case: 200k units a year (~$4.8M revenue, like Gaon Lab and Yeoreum) at 32% ACoS, fixed costs unchanged.

slides.title: The Japan scale-up is safe but small: $7M of added revenue by 2030, in a market growing 1.5% a year, and it leaves the US untouched

claims.claim: Added revenue by year, $M
A vs J comparison
evidence: Market growth: US K-beauty ~17%/yr vs Japan facial ~1.5%/yr
Starting position: New; pilot only vs 3.1% share today

claims.claim: If ACoS runs at 32%, J returns more cash by 2030. But it adds only $7M of revenue and does nothing for the US ambition. A builds a $26M business still growing ~30% a year. Keep J on the list for 2028 or later, once the US team is running.

slides.title: No route reaches $40M by 2030 within the board's limits. Keep the limits and move the $40M milestone to about 2032

claims.claim: Not recommended: Keep "$40M in 2030". Only B gets close ($37.6M), and only by breaking the cash cap, the payback test and the margin floor, on inputs that look optimistic.
Recommended: Keep the limits, move the date. A reaches ~$26M in 2030. At +25% a year it passes $40M around 2032, sooner if the retail gates (next page) are met.
evidence: 2031–32 is an illustrative extension at +25% a year (below the plan's +29% in 2030); it is not a planning-team forecast.

slides.title: Add retail later, through tighter gates: awareness above 20% (not 15%) and a first step the group margin can absorb

claims.claim: Awareness gate: 20% or more aided awareness among all facial-skincare buyers (today 4%) vs CEO's draft above 15%
evidence: At 10–20% awareness newcomers sell a median 3.5 units/door/week (IQR 2.8–4.3): most fall below the 4.0 removal bar. Above 20% the median is 4.6.

claims.claim: Amazon scale gate: $20M or more a year at ACoS of 30% or less vs CEO's draft Amazon sales above $10M
evidence: Retail's fixed costs need a profitable base. Saebom reached ~$30M before adding doors. On plan, A reaches $20M in 2029.

claims.claim: First step: A test of ~300 doors, with a budget below the margin headroom (CEO's draft not specified; board member proposes 600 doors nationally)
evidence: In 2030, group profit above the 8% floor is only $3.9–5.7M. B's retail leg costs $4.4–7.2M a year more than A.

claims.claim: Timing: When the gates are met, which means planning for 2030 at the earliest (CEO's draft from 2029)
evidence: Awareness has to rise five-fold from 4%. Track it every six months from the 2027 launch.

slides.title: Approve the Amazon-led launch with a $4M cash envelope and guardrails that bring the decision back to the board early

claims.claim: Decisions requested
evidence: 1 Enter the US in 2027 via the Amazon-led route. No 600-door retail launch; no Japan scale-up in 2027
2 Authorise up to $4M of cumulative US cash outflow. Any need beyond that returns to the board
3 Accept that 2030 payback is at risk. On plan if ACoS ≤ 28.6%; at 32% ACoS, about 2032
4 Reset the ambition: $40M as a 2031–32 milestone; add retail only through the gates on page 14

claims.claim: Guardrails, reviewed quarterly (Metric / Plan / Review trigger)
evidence: Blended ACoS / ≤ 28% / Above 32% for two quarters in a row
Cumulative US cash / $1.9M peak on plan / Outflow passes $4M
Amazon units / 300k in 2027 / Below 200k annualised by Q4 2027
90-day repeat / ≥ 31% benchmark / Still ≤ 29% after US labels and new SKUs
US duty on Korean cosmetics / 15% / Rises to 25% (mid-2027 decision): re-plan, break-even ACoS 26.9%

claims.claim: The $4M envelope covers the 32% ACoS + 25% duty case (peak −$3.9M).

slides.title: How the options were modelled: the planning team's inputs, applied consistently, with benchmark cases added

claims.claim: Per-unit contribution (hero product, applied to all SKUs as the planning team does)
evidence: Amazon: $24.00 − 15% referral − $5.10 FBA − $3.50 product − $0.55 freight − 15% duty on product − ACoS × price = $4.73 at 25% ACoS
Retail: $14.00 wholesale − $3.50 − $0.75 freight − $0.53 duty − 8% co-op − 4% returns = $7.55
Retail volume = doors × 4.5 units × 52 weeks; B Amazon units = A × 1.3

claims.claim: Costs and cash
evidence: Fixed and one-time costs per Table 6; fixtures $1,100 for each new door in the year it opens
Inventory held = 4 months of that year's landed cost (product + freight + duty); cash flow = operating profit − increase in inventory
Option J: revenue × 30% − $0.8M a year − $1.0M one-time; no working capital given, so none included

claims.claim: Board tests
evidence: Peak cash = lowest cumulative cash flow, 2027–30
Group margin = (ex-US plan revenue × 11% + option operating profit) ÷ (ex-US revenue + option revenue)

claims.claim: Cases
evidence: Benchmark: 32% ACoS, the agency median for $5M→$20M brands; range 26–38% tested
Tariff: duty 25% on product cost, applied to all four years (a conservative stress)
Not modelled: FX (a weaker won would help), tax, cost inflation, post-2030 terminal value

slides.title: Choices made without the CEO's input, and how each affects the answer

claims.claim: "On the way to $40M by 2030" read as a direction, not a hard limit. The four numeric limits (cap, payback, margin, bandwidth) are treated as binding.
evidence: If $40M in 2030 were binding, no option passes; B still breaks three limits.

claims.claim: Onsoo's awareness taken as 4% (all facial-skincare buyers), matching Table 8's "category buyers".
evidence: At 9% (K-beauty buyers) Onsoo is still in the lowest band; conclusion unchanged.

claims.claim: 32% used as the main stress case, because A's revenue path ($7M→$26M) matches the benchmark's $5M→$20M brands.
evidence: Turns A's payback from "pass" to "at risk"; cap and margin still pass.

claims.claim: A duty of 25% applied to all years, though a decision is due only in mid-2027.
$4M cash envelope set to cover the 32% ACoS + 25% duty case (peak $3.9M); our proposal, not a board figure.
evidence: Board may prefer a different number; the $18M cap is untouched.

claims.claim: Retail gates: 20% awareness, $20M Amazon sales, ~300-door test: drawn from Table 8, Saebom and the margin headroom.
evidence: These are proposals for the board to confirm.

claims.claim: 2031–32 extension: +25% a year after 2030, for illustration only.
evidence: Only affects when $40M is reached, not the 2027 decision.

claims.claim: These were made in the absence of client input and should be confirmed before the board meeting.

normalized.recommendation: Approve Option A (Amazon-led) for 2027 with a $4M US cash envelope. Reject Option B (600-door retail launch) and defer Option J (Japan scale-up). Add specialty retail only once aided awareness passes 20%. Accept that 2030 payback is at risk; reset the ambition: $40M as a 2031–32 milestone; add retail only through the gates on page 14 (20%+ aided awareness, $20M+ Amazon sales at ACoS ≤30%, ~300-door test).

alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen. Only route that fits within the board's limits: peak −$1.9M (−$3.2M at 32% ACoS), lowest-year group margin 9.5%; payback at risk (+$2.4M at 25% ACoS, −$2.3M at 32% ACoS); reaches $26.4M in 2030.

Rejected. Breaks the $18M cap (−$20.8M peak), never pays back and takes group margin below 8% for three years (4.5%/6.6%/7.5%), even on planning-team inputs; inputs are optimistic (2.6 units/door/week at Onsoo's awareness vs 4.5 assumed, 4.0 removal bar; halo is correlation not cause); realistic inputs give −$31M. Mooncrest precedent est. $21M loss.

Deferred. Safe but small: $7M added revenue by 2030 in a market growing 1.5% a year; does nothing for the US ambition. If ACoS runs at 32%, J returns more cash by 2030. Keep J on the list for 2028 or later, once the US team is running.
Not recommended. Only B gets close ($37.6M), and only by breaking the cash cap, the payback test and the margin floor.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the limits, move the date (~2032)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended. A reaches ~$26M in 2030; at +25% a year it passes $40M around 2032.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO's draft retail gates (awareness >15%, Amazon sales >$10M, from 2029) / board member's 600 doors nationally
alternatives_considered.treatment: Replaced by tighter gates: 20%+ awareness, $20M+ Amazon sales at ACoS ≤30%, ~300-door test within margin headroom, planning for 2030 at the earliest.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: All company, competitor and market figures in the pack are synthetic benchmark data.
Prepared from the planning-team briefing pack only (no outside research).
Payback by 2030 holds only if ACoS stays at or below 28.6%. At the 32% scaling benchmark it slips to about 2032.
The plan assumes ACoS falls to 25%; the benchmark says it rises with scale as click costs climb (median 32%, range 26–38%).
Break-even ACoS falls to 26.9% if duty rises to 25% (tariff decision mid-2027); tariff stress applied to all four years (conservative).
2027 plan needs 300k units = 1.8× the June run-rate; relies on four new SKUs, and monthly growth slowed from 16–17% to 8–9%.
Amazon-first does not guarantee scale: two of three peers stayed below $5M; stall case costs ~$7.1M peak.
Per-unit economics of the hero product applied to all SKUs as the planning team does.
Not modelled: FX (a weaker won would help), tax, cost inflation, post-2030 terminal value.
2031–32 is an illustrative extension at +25% a year; it is not a planning-team forecast.
"On the way to $40M by 2030" read as a direction, not a hard limit; four numeric limits treated as binding.
Onsoo's awareness taken as 4% (all facial-skincare buyers); at 9% (K-beauty buyers) conclusion unchanged.
$4M envelope and retail gates are proposals, not board figures; judgment calls made without client input should be confirmed before the board meeting.
Halo: the 0.71 link between doors and Amazon sales is correlation, not cause.
next_steps: Set up the US entity and MoCRA registration
Take the listings over from the cross-border seller
First awareness survey in Q3 (track awareness every six months from the 2027 launch)
Review guardrails quarterly (ACoS, cumulative cash, Amazon units, 90-day repeat, US duty, aided awareness)
Confirm judgment calls with the CEO before the board meeting
normalized.extraction_notes: The deck was supplied as plain text with no images. Chart values come from the text extraction, so where a number belongs in a chart was worked out from the order the text appears in. In particular, the per-unit waterfall on slide 7 and the bar and line values on slides 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 were matched to their labels by sequence. On slide 2, the executive summary's three column headings ("The US is worth entering", "Only Amazon-led fits the board's limits", "What the board has to accept") were joined to the points beneath them. The governing thought is the title of slide 2, the executive summary slide. The cover title on slide 1 states a related headline: "US entry in 2027: go in through Amazon, and earn the way into specialty retail".
